headline: G2 GOLDFIELDS PUNCHES OKO TO 1KM DEPTH: 84.5m at 3.0 g/t Au — C$3B buyer watches resource grow
snippet: G2 Goldfields drilled its deepest hole yet at Guyana's OKO Project, returning 84.5m at 3.0 g/t gold from 915m depth — with a separate infill hole hitting 20.8m at 9.6 g/t including 4.4m at 36.1 g/t — extending the deposit to 1km vertical while eight rigs continue infill and expansion work. The results land mid-deal as G Mining Ventures works toward closing its C$3B all-share acquisition of G2.

headline: LION ZONE DELIVERS: Power Metallic hits 17.45m at 9.47% CuEq, Nisk MRE on deck
snippet: Power Metallic Mines (TSX-V: PNPN) intercepted 17.45m at 9.47% copper-equivalent at its Lion Zone in Quebec — including a 6.30m section grading 17.91% CuEq — and followed up with 39m at 5.66% CuEq in a second hole 100m east. The winter 2026 infill program at the Nisk polymetallic project is building the dataset for a 2026 Mineral Resource Estimate.

headline: NGEx DISCOVERS NEW HIGH-GRADE ZONE at Lunahuasi: 23m at 4.72% CuEq found 300m East of Mars
snippet: NGEx Minerals wrapped Phase 4 drilling at its Lunahuasi copper-gold project in Argentina with two standout Mars Zone holes — 34m at 7.25% CuEq and 48m at 7.72% CuEq, 180m apart — then discovered an entirely new zone 300m to the east, where the first hole returned 23m at 4.72% CuEq including 4.20m at 17.94% CuEq. The 27,318m Phase 4 program is now complete.

headline: SIXTH STRAIGHT YEAR: Silver deficit widens 15% to 46.3M oz — cumulative six-year gap hits 762M oz
snippet: The Silver Institute's World Silver Survey 2026 projects a sixth consecutive annual market deficit of 46.3 million troy ounces — 15% wider than 2025 — bringing the cumulative six-year drawdown to 762 million ounces. Demand is holding firm: China imported a record 836 tonnes of silver in March alone, 173% above the 10-year seasonal average, driven by solar manufacturing stockpiling and a retail investment surge.

headline: BANK OF AMERICA HOLDS $6,000 GOLD TARGET — sees silver averaging $86 in 2026
snippet: Bank of America reiterated its 12-month $6,000/oz gold price target and forecast silver will average $86 in 2026, with scope to peak between $135 and $309 at the cycle top. The bank frames gold as the 'primary hedge and performance driver' of 2026 while pointing to solar and EV demand as silver's separate structural bid alongside central bank and retail buying.

headline: COPPER AT $5.94/LB, UP 25% YoY: June tariff ruling could push prices to new record
snippet: Copper climbed to $5.94/lb on May 5 — up 2.44% on the session and 25% year-on-year — as US importers stockpile 450,000–830,000 tonnes ahead of a Trump administration tariff decision expected in June. Chile's sulphur supply disruption is squeezing physical availability, while data centre and grid electrification demand shows no sign of softening.

headline: WHO'S WINNING THE 2026 EXPLORATION RACE? TSX-V juniors lead the global discovery sprint
snippet: Junior miners are outspending majors on grass-roots exploration per dollar of market cap in 2026, with TSX-V and ASX companies leading drill campaigns across Africa, South America, and the Athabasca Basin. The analysis examines which geologies are attracting the most risk capital and where the next generation of resource discoveries is most likely to emerge.

headline: USA RARE EARTH'S $2.8B BRAZIL BET: Can Serra Verde break China's rare earth monopoly?
snippet: USA Rare Earth's $2.8 billion agreement to acquire Brazil's Serra Verde — the only large-scale non-Asian producer of all four magnetic rare earths including critical heavy elements dysprosium, terbium, and yttrium — is being framed as the most significant challenge yet to China's 70% grip on mine output and 85% of global refining. The Diplomat asks whether the deal can reorient supply chains or merely relocates existing bottlenecks.

headline: AI BOOM TURBOCHARGES Uranium Demand — Nuclear Fuel Supply Crunch Deepens in 2026
snippet: Uranium spot prices hit $100/lb in early 2026 — up 25% in January alone — as AI data centre operators lock in nuclear power purchase agreements and global reactor construction backlogs grow. The US government's $2.7 billion enrichment investment and Section 232 critical minerals designation add policy support to a market already strained by constrained mine supply.

headline: LITHIUM'S RECOVERY TAKES HOLD: Energy Storage Set to Consume 31% of Global Supply in 2026
snippet: Battery storage demand for lithium is set to reach 31% of all consumption in 2026 — up from 23% in 2025 — as China's power sector reforms fuel grid-scale storage buildout. Australia's March lithium loadings hit a record 488,200 tonnes as spodumene prices recover from cycle lows, with producers like Core Lithium restarting operations placed on care and maintenance during the 2024 price collapse.
